t: A Central African kingdom south of the lower Congo River, ruled from Mbanza Kongo by an elected manikongo.
It was among the first African states to sustain diplomacy with Europe, adopting Christianity and Portuguese literacy.
The Atlantic slave trade fuelled rivalries, and defeat at Mbwila in 1665 tipped it into civil war and long decline.
dyk: Kongo used nzimbu shells, gathered on the royal fishery of Luanda Island, as currency alongside squares of finely woven raffia cloth.
ev: Portuguese navigator Diogo Cao reaches the mouth of the Congo
King Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised as Joao I
Afonso I wins the throne by defeating his half-brother Mpanzu a Kitima
Afonso I writes to Joao III of Portugal protesting the abuses of the slave trade
Jaga invaders drive Alvaro I from his capital until Portuguese troops restore him
Portuguese forces defeat Kongo at Mbwila, killing King Antonio I
Beatriz Kimpa Vita, leader of the Antonian movement, is executed
Pedro IV reoccupies Sao Salvador and nominally reunifies the kingdom
